source: Copies of four selected compiled UI archives from /Applications/TickTick.app; no reference application code was executed.
limitations: The graph reflects recognized Interface Builder archive fields and connections; omitted private or unrecognized archive fields remain unknown.
A target-action selector is an Interface Builder observation and does not prove that the binary contains a matching implementation.
Decoded constraints, runtime visibility, dynamic UI creation, and pixel geometry are not inferred from these archives.

Compiled Interface Builder archives are private serialized object graphs. The decoder reports only recognized keyed-archive objects and connections; unrecognized object classes and fields remain unknown.
conclusions: The tag editor declares name, color and parent controls in the same archive.
The filter editor declares a segmented control and save/cancel controls.
These declarations do not establish runtime visibility, exact geometry, advanced expression precedence or gesture rules.
